chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr and Fudayl and Burayd and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them); among them is he who narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and among them is he who narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and among them is he who narrated from one of them (peace be upon them both).

That the wife does not inherit from her husband's estate from the plaster of a house or land, unless the brick, logs, and wood are appraised at a value, so she is given one-quarter or one-eighth of it, if it is from the value of the brick, logs, and wood.
ai.seo_question: How is a wife's share of the house calculated in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This narration from the Ahl al-Bayt clarifies the distinction between land and structure in inheritance, specifying that the wife receives a fraction of the appraised value of the building materials (turba, wood) rather than the land itself. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that the 'house' (dar) comprises both the plot and the edifice, with the wife's share limited to the latter's value. It highlights the practical application of Quranic inheritance verses by detailing how to calculate shares when the asset is a mixed property.
